data.long_meaning: Iblis is considered the name of the angel who refused to bow before Adam, leading to his expulsion from heaven and transformation into Satan. In Christian tradition, Iblis is not considered evil, but rather a symbol of disobedience and free will. The name Iblis carries the meaning “Rebel Angel” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Iblis usually hope their child will grow to embody rebel angel and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iblis total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: איבליס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: איבליס הוא שם שמופיע בקוראן ובמסורות מוסלמיות, ומתייחס לשטן או ללוציפר. אין לו שימוש ישיר בתנ"ך העברי או בברית החדשה, אך הוא קשור למושגים של רוע ומרידה נגד האל. השם איבליס עצמו עשוי להיות קשור לשורשים ערביים ומוסלמיים, אך הוא מוכר גם בקהילות נוצריות כמונח המתאר את השטן או את הנפיל.

in_greek.name: Ιμπλיס
in_greek.meaning: Όνομα συνώνυμο του Σατανά, εχθρός του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιμπλיס εμφανίζεται στο Κοράνι και στις μουσουλμανικές παραδόσεις, αναφερόμενο στον Σατανά ή τον Λουσιφύρο. Δεν υπάρχει άμεση χρήση στη Βίβλο ή στη Νέα Διαθήκη, αλλά συνδέεται με έννοιες κακού και εξέγερσης ενάντια στον Θεό. Το ίδιο το όνομα Ιμπλיס μπορεί να έχει αραβικές και μουσουλμανικές ρίζες, αλλά είναι γνωστό και στις χριστιανικές κοινότητες ως όρος που περιγράφει τον Σατανά ή την πτώση.

in_latin.name: Iblis
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Iblis in Corano et traditionibus musulmanis apparet, et ad Satanam vel Luciferum refertur. Non est usus directus in Bibliis Hebraeis vel Novo Testamento, sed coniungitur cum conceptibus malorum et rebellionis contra Deum. Ipsum nomen Iblis possit habere radices arabicas et musulmanas, sed etiam in communitatibus christianis notum est ut terminus qui Satanam vel lapsum describit.

in_english.name: Iblis
in_english.meaning: A synonym for Satan, the adversary of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Iblis appears in the Quran and Muslim traditions, referring to Satan or Lucifer. There is no direct usage in the Hebrew Bible or New Testament, but it is associated with concepts of evil and rebellion against God. The name Iblis itself may have Arabic and Muslim roots, but it is also recognized in Christian communities as a term describing Satan or the Fall. Historically, Iblis has been used interchangeably with Satan in various religious texts and traditions, symbolizing the embodiment of evil and opposition to divine will.

data.cultural_impact: The name Iblis carries significant historical and cultural weight, originating from Islamic and Jewish traditions. Although primarily associated with Islamic folklore, certain aspects of the Iblis story have seeped into the Western consciousness through various forms of media, literature, and academic study. As a result, the name carries a sense of intrigue and fascination, inspiring artists, writers, and scholars to explore the complexities of human obedience, free will, and the darker aspects of the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, Iblis represents an important reminder of the fundamental importance of obedience and submission to God's will. While the early Christian tradition did not have a fixed doctrine on the origin of Satan, the Iblis story can be interpreted as a cautionary tale of the consequences of disobedience, pride, and rebellion against the divine will. Iblis serves as a reminder that even angels, despite their celestial status, can fall from grace when they choose to prioritize their own desires over submission to God's plan. Ultimately, the story of Iblis underscores the value of humility, obedience, and faith in the face of adversity and temptation.
